To implement a Predictive Risk Classification Architecture (with mDeBERTa-v3, GoEmotions classifier, and FAISS recurrence model) that analyzes text-based data inputs and detects psychological distress indicators to predict the likelihood of risk escalations, apart from the normal risk categories of Low, Medium, High, and facCritical.
Multi-Level Severity and Risk Classification in Text-Based Cyberbullying and Distress Detection

According to Malam et al. (2020), traditional binary classification models that merely label text as "bullying" or "non-bullying" fail to provide actionable context for institutional intervention. In their study, machine learning classifiers were trained to categorize text into four distinct severity levels (None, Low, Medium, and High), demonstrating that multi-level severity scoring allows responders to differentiate routine insults from high-harm threats. Complementing this, EMNLP Findings (2022) and Fodeh et al. (2022) applied natural language processing to stratify text-based psychological distress into four risk tiers (Low, Moderate/Medium, High, and Critical/Severe). Their research highlighted that isolating a dedicated Critical tier is essential for identifying emergency scenarios such as explicit self-harm or severe harassment that necessitate immediate escalation and intervention.

StudentShield adopts this exact multi-level risk architecture by mapping analyzed student entries into four structured risk bands: Low (1%–30%), Medium (31%–60%), High (61%–85%), and Critical (86%–100%). By combining sentiment analysis, emotion classification, and heuristic rule triggers, StudentShield ensures that low-level venting is logged appropriately, while entries reaching the Critical threshold automatically trigger real-time SMS and email alerts to parents and guidance counselors for prompt intervention.
